newsitem.title: FRANCE: World fx levels normalising, may last -Camdessus.
newsitem.headline: World fx levels normalising, may last -Camdessus.

text.p: International Monetary Fund chief Michel Camdessus said in an interview in the French daily Le Monde on Friday that he believed world currency levels were normalising and could last.
"It is not surprising that the dollar is so robust at the time when the American economy itself is strong," he said

"This leads me to believe that there is a normalisation of the international monetary constellation which has a chance of lasting because it is based on fundamental elements," Le Monde quoted Camdessus as telling its Washington correspondent in an interview.

International Monetary Fund managing director Michel Camdessus said in an interview on Friday 1997 was set to be a year of stable world growth, outside Europe, without an acceleration of inflation and that this could last four or five years.

"For the world with the exception of Europe, 1997 looks set to be a year of stable growth without an acceleration of inflation," he was quoted by daily Le Monde as saying in an interview. "Also, there is a good chance that, with constant policy, such a phenomenon can last during the four or five coming years," Camdessus was quoted as saying.
